truth: Morrowind is the Dunmer homeland: the island of Vvardenfell, with the volcano Red Mountain at its heart, and the mainland beyond the Inner Sea, walled from Skyrim and Cyrodiil by the Velothi and Valus ranges. Its people worship the Tribunal, three living gods who rule from Vivec, Mournhold and a hidden city, and honour their own ancestors whose bones guard every family. Five Great Houses split the land: the Hlaalu traders, the Redoran warriors and the Telvanni wizards on Vvardenfell; the Indoril priest-nobles and the Dres slave-planters on the mainland. The Empire keeps forts and a trading charter it calls an alliance, while ash storms carry a plague out of the mountain.

vvardenfell_ashlands.truth: The Ashlands are grey volcanic country north and west of Red Mountain, swept by choking storms that bury roads and cairns in hours. Ald'ruhn, the Vvardenfell seat of House Redoran, is built inside and around Skar, the hollowed shell of a giant ancient emperor crab, and its warrior-nobles hold the northern frontier by duty and austere pride. Maar Gan's pilgrim shrine, Gnisis' rich egg mine, Khuul and Ald Velothi's fishing harbours, the Urshilaku Ashlander nomads and Fort Buckmoth all scrape a living from the ash while Sixth House sleepers gather in ruined Kogoruhn.

west_gash.truth: The West Gash is a belt of rocky limestone ridges and green river valleys along Vvardenfell's western flank, where the Odai River runs through Balmora, the bustling Hlaalu seat of yellow plaster terraces, guild halls and merchant manors. Upriver, the Empire's chartered company town of Caldera digs rich ebony in stone towers built in Cyrodilic style. House Hlaalu does business with the Empire and anyone else, while the Camonna Tong crime syndicate runs the docks and hates the outlanders who own the mines. Above the valley, Dwemer Arkngthand and Foyada Mamaea scar the hills.

bitter_coast.truth: The Bitter Coast is a warm, rotting swamp shore along Vvardenfell's south-west, a maze of twisted bog trees, brackish mudflats, glowing mushroom caps and thick sea fog. At its southern gate, Seyda Neen's Imperial Census and Excise warehouse and wooden lighthouse greet prisoners and merchants arriving from Cyrodiil, while the stilted shacks of Hla Oad and Gnaar Mok make more coin from smuggling than from netch or fish. Sea caves along the inlets hide skooma, moon sugar and escaped slaves, and sunken Daedric ruins rot in the mangrove mire.

ascadian_isles.truth: The Ascadian Isles are Vvardenfell's green, fertile southern garden: placid lakes, emperor-parasol groves, bridged channels and the great water city of Vivec, where nine stepped cantons stand in the bay below the floating Ministry of Truth and the palace of the living god. Around Lake Amaya and Lake Masobi lie walled Hlaalu and Dres saltrice plantations worked by Argonian and Khajiit slaves, alongside Pelagiad's Imperial fort, Suran's hillside pleasure houses and the pilgrim shrines of the Seven Graces. The wealth here is old, the cruelty is polite, and Twin Lamps abolitionists move in secret.

azuras_coast.truth: Azura's Coast is Vvardenfell's jagged eastern archipelago: hundreds of steep basalt islets, kelp-choked channels and giant fungal towers facing the sunrise over the Padomaic sea. Tel Branora at the southern point, Tel Aruhn with its underground slave market, and Tel Fyr—where the four-thousand-year-old wizard Divayth Fyr keeps his Corprusarium for the incurably blighted—rise from the islands. Hidden behind a magical rock door on a southern island, the Dissident Priests of Holamayan preserve the history the Tribunal suppresses, while Azura's great twilight statue watches from the headland cliffs.

molag_amur.truth: Molag Amur is a black wasteland of lava fields, cinder cones and boiling fumaroles south-east of Red Mountain, the harshest country on Vvardenfell outside the Ghostfence. Molag Mar, a fortified adobe canton town shared by the Temple and House Redoran, is the sole settlement; the rest belongs to the Erabenimsun, the fiercest and most warlike of the four Ashlander tribes. Pilgrims cross its burning passes to reach the holy peaks of Mount Assarnibibi and Mount Kand. Fire ferns glow beside the lava vents, kagouti stalk the ravines, and Daedra haunt the basalt shrines.

grazelands.truth: The Grazelands are a rolling green steppe across Vvardenfell's north-east, sheltered in the lee of the northern hills to form the only open herding country on the island. Wild wickwheat and hackle-lo leaf carpet the plains, where the Zainab and Ahemmusa Ashlander tribes drive their guar herds from spring to spring. Into this nomad pasture the Telvanni have pushed the farming village of Vos and the hybrid stone-and-fungus fortress of Tel Vos, ruled by Master Aryon, the youngest and most reform-minded Telvanni councillor. Beneath the grass, ten kwama mines are falling silent as Blight creeps down from the mountain.

sheogorad.truth: Sheogorad is a cold, storm-battered archipelago of jagged rock islands and treacherous reefs off Vvardenfell's northern coast, named for the Mad God. Its sole town is Dagon Fel, a bleak fishing and salvage harbour settled by hardy Nords who trade across the Sea of Ghosts with Skyrim and strip the shipwrecks that litter every shoal. Across the rocky channels stand solitary Velothi wizard towers, the remote Sanctus Shrine where Temple pilgrims keep a vow of silence, and the sprawling island fortress-shrine of Ald Daedroth, where Sheogorath's cultists and Ordinators war amid the surf.

red_mountain.truth: Red Mountain is Vvardenfell's smoking volcanic heart, encircled by the Tribunal's Ghostfence—a shimmering blue wall of ancestor-bone wards raised to quarantine the Blight and the awakened Sixth House. Inside the fence, red ash storms howl without cease over black cinder slopes, foyada lava chutes and Dwemer citadels held by Dagoth Ur and his ash-vampire brothers. Nothing grows here but blight-twisted scrub, corprus beasts and eyeless ash creatures. Ghostgate, the twin-towered fortress spanning the only pass through the fence, is the sole lawful outpost, garrisoned by Ordinators and Buoyant Armigers whose wards grow weaker every month.

zafirbel_bay.truth: Zafirbel Bay is the island-studded eastern bay of Vvardenfell, the insular heartland of House Telvanni on the island. Its seat, Sadrith Mora, is a forest of giant grown emperor-mushroom towers linked by spiraling root ramps and vertical levitation shafts where the Telvanni Council meets. Outsiders are confined to the Gateway Inn or to Wolverine Hall, an Imperial Legion fortress bolted directly onto the side of the bay to house the Empire's guilds and chapel. Across the surrounding coral reefs and islets rise rival wizard spires like Tel Naga and steaming Dwemer sea pipes, in a bay where might is law.

telvannis.truth: The Telvanni Peninsula is the mainland's wild, cliff-walled north-eastern arm, a realm of giant coastal mushroom forests, black sand beaches and archmagisters who answer neither to the Grand Council nor to the Empire. At its northern tip stands Port Telvannis, the ancient mainland seat of House Telvanni and a harbour of immense fungal spires; to the west rises Firewatch, an Imperial-chartered walled beacon city keeping a lighthouse flame over the stormy cape. Between them lie mist-wrapped spore glades, rogue wizard experiments and deep Dwemer steam-works, while Telvanni galleys ship slaves and enchanted wares down the coast.

stonefalls.truth: Stonefalls is the mainland's volcanic western march, stretching from the snow-dusted Velothi foothills at Blacklight down to Old Ebonheart on the Inner Sea and Kragenmoor by the Valus passes into Cyrodiil. Ebonheart is the hinge between Empire and province: a fortress-city holding the Imperial garrison, the East Empire Company's main hall and the Grand Council chamber where the five Great Houses meet. Smoking lava shields, basalt columns and the twin peaks of the Brothers of Strife dominate the interior, while Redoran border keeps watch Skyrim, Hlaalu ships crowd Davon's Watch, and Dhalmora remembers the Second Era Pact.

deshaan.truth: Deshaan is the rich southern heartland of mainland Morrowind: wide bioluminescent fungal plains, obsidian gorges and misty lagoons surrounding Mournhold, the white-and-gold sacred capital of the goddess Almalexia, the nominal Imperial King of Morrowind, and House Indoril. Beneath Mournhold's concentric plazas lie the buried ruins of Old Mournhold and the Dwemer weather-foundry of Bamz-Amschend. To the east, Tear sits in the feverish border marshes as the capital of House Dres and the province's largest slave market; to the west, Narsis anchors Hlaalu trade on the river, making Deshaan wealthy and uneasy.

necrom.truth: The Necrom Coast is mainland Morrowind's solemn south-eastern seaboard, a pale landscape of limestone tomb-terraces, basalt sea spires and lantern-lit processional roads given wholly to the dead. At its centre stands Necrom, the white-walled City of the Dead, where Dunmer families of every Great House bring their ancestors' ashes and bones by barge and bier to be entombed by the Keepers of the Dead. Funeral harbours at Zaappi and Elamasipal live off mourners and pilgrims, while deep beneath the catacombs, bone-thieving necromancers and seekers of Hermaeus Mora's forbidden libraries pry into vaults meant never to open.

forbidden.reason: Scorched cinder waste inside the Ghostfence cannot sustain flooded saltrice paddies
Morrowind has no broadleaf or conifer timber mills outside the Velothi foothills; Ashlands grow only fungi and scrub
Necrom's sacred catacombs are governed strictly by Dunmer ancestor and Tribunal rites, not Imperial cathedrals
